subject: Pilot activation: mutual checkpoints & acceptance tests
messages:
From: Elena Moreno <elena@medsync.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot scope & timeline — Medsync MVP evaluation

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput and token-cost figures looked promising. We're interested in running a 6-week pilot focused on clinical note summarization and triage routing.

High level ask: can Redwood provide a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that lays out acceptance tests, exit gates, and the timeline so we can align stakeholders (clinical ops, security, procurement)? Procurement will need a clear runbook and SOC2 evidence.

I've attached a short MVP requirements doc so you can see the baseline success criteria we care about.

Attachments: Medsync_MVP_requirements.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Elena Moreno
Head of Product, Medsync Health
elena@medsync.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Moreno <elena@medsync.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot scope & timeline — Medsync MVP evaluation

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear brief and the attachment.

We can absolutely put together a MAP with acceptance tests and exit gates. Quick note on approach: we propose a 4-week technical validation (functional correctness, latency & throughput at target load, safety/concordance sampling) followed by a 2-week operational handoff (cutover run, monitoring smoke-tests, training and runbook delivery).

Grace and Marissa — can you review the MVP attachment and add any Redwood-specific acceptance checks we should include (security evidence, SLA targets, rollback triggers)?

Elena — we'll aim to send a draft MAP by Thu 5/20 so procurement has something to review early next week.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: internal: Pilot acceptance checks (draft items)

Jonas / Grace — internal checklist ideas below (short bullets) we can port into the MAP:

- Acceptance tests (functional):
  * End-to-end summary F1 >= 0.77 on curated clinical holdout (Elena's MVP doc): priority pass/fail.
  * Triage routing accuracy >= 85% for priority classes.
  * No PII leakage on 1000-sample token scan.

- Performance & reliability:
  * 95th percentile token latency <= 120ms at target concurrency (50 rps steady-state).
  * KV prefix cache hit >= 20% for templated notes.

- Safety & concordance:
  * Human review concordance >= 90% for 200 sampled cases.
  * Explicit fail if hallucination rate > 2% by defined metric.

- Operational:
  * SOC2 evidence packet (summary doc) delivered to procurement by week 2.
  * Monitoring dashboard (latency, cost per 1k tokens, error rate) available in Redwood Console.
  * Rollback plan: immediate model fallback to smaller model + traffic shift policy.

I'll mock these into the map doc and attach the first draft.

Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Moreno <elena@medsync.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T11:34:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood MAP draft: Medsync pilot — acceptance tests & exit gates (draft attached)

Elena — attaching the draft Mutual Action Plan. Key highlights in the email below.

Attachments: redwood_map_draft.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Summary of the MAP (high level):
- Weeks 1–4 (Validation):
  * W1: Integration & baseline smoke tests (connectors, data flow, signing of test dataset NDA).
  * W2: Functional testing + safety sampling (Marissa's concordance checks + hallucination metric).
  * W3: Performance run (load tests to confirm 95p latency and throughput).
  * W4: Acceptance window — run acceptance tests across 1,000 representative notes.
- Weeks 5–6 (Handoff):
  * W5: Operational run, dashboard handover, runbook and playbook sign-off.
  * W6: Final sign-off: procurement + clinical ops sign acceptance; optional extension/rollout discussion.

Exit gates (examples):
- Functional gate: E2E summary F1 >= 0.77 AND triage accuracy >= 85%.
- Performance gate: 95p latency <= 120ms and error rate < 1%.
- Security gate: SOC2 summary and PII scan report submitted.

Owners: Redwood (Jonas, Marissa — delivery), Medsync (Elena, Clinical Ops lead), Procurement (procurement@medsync.com).

Request: Please review the acceptance thresholds and let us know if any items need to move (e.g., stricter concordance or a replaced metric). If procurement prefers a separate lane for contract redlines, we can spin up a procurement-only appendix.

Thanks — expect a version 1.1 after procurement's note.

Jonas
From: Elena Moreno <elena@medsync.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Medsync Procurement <procurement@medsync.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T10:16:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MAP draft: Medsync pilot — acceptance tests & exit gates (draft attached)

Jonas — this is very helpful, thank you. A few comments from clinical ops and procurement below:

Clinical ops (short):
- Move the concordance sample to 300 cases (stat power).
- Add a real-world edge-case bucket (hand-transcribed notes).

Procurement (procurement@medsync.com):
- We need the SOC2 summary by week 2 and a short note on data residency / retention.
- Please add a clause for a 30-day remediation window if the pilot fails any critical exit gate before the final sign-off.

I've attached the SOC2 summary we usually ask vendors to include (format). Can you confirm Redwood can provide a short summary by the end of week 2?

Attachments: SOC2_summary.docx

Thanks,
Elena
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Moreno <elena@medsync.com>, Medsync Procurement <procurement@medsync.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-24T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MAP draft: Medsync pilot — acceptance tests & exit gates (draft attached)

Elena / team — appreciate the quick feedback. Acceptance updates and next steps below: 

1) Acceptance thresholds updated: concordance sample = 300, edge-case bucket included (hand-transcribed).
2) Security deliverable: Redwood will provide a SOC2 summary packet and data retention note by 2027-05-27 (within week 2).
3) Remediation clause: we will include a 30-day remediation window for any failed critical gate — owners and rollback steps spelled out in the procurement appendix.

Finalized timeline (agreed):
- 2027-05-31: Test dataset NDA signed + integration smoke pass.
- 2027-06-07: End of week 2 security & functional milestone (SOC2 summary delivered).
- 2027-06-21: Completion of validation runs (end of W4) + acceptance test results delivered.
- 2027-06-28: Final sign-off meeting (procurement + clinical ops).

Next actions: Marissa will circulate the MAP v1.2 with the updated thresholds and the procurement appendix by EOD 5/25. Elena — please confirm procurement availability for the 6/28 sign-off meeting.

Cheers,
Jonas
